header: Headway helps therapists take insurance, so more people can afford therapy. Fresh off a $100M raise, the team was ready to give the product therapists use every day a facelift. I redesigned the tools that keep a practice running, from the calendar to client assessments.
seo_description: Product design case study: redesigning the tools therapists use to run their practice on Headway, the mental health network that helps therapists take insurance.

media.name: therapy_1.png
media.title: The home screen, with the day’s to-dos up front

layout.title: Start with what’s due
text: A therapist’s day is full of sessions, not software. Home opens on a short to-do list, with sessions to confirm and clients to follow up with, so nothing slips between appointments.

media.name: therapy_2.png
media.title: The calendar, with sessions and open slots side by side

layout.title: The week at a glance
text: The calendar shows booked sessions, open slots, and whether each one is video, phone, or in person. A busy week is easy to scan.

media.name: therapy_3.png
media.title: The form library, with every consent form in one place

layout.title: Paperwork, handled
text: Consent forms and intake questionnaires live in one library. Save a form once, and it goes out automatically to every new client.

media.name: therapy_4.png
media.title: Adding a form, with the option to upload one you already use

layout.title: Bring your own forms
text: Therapists can start from scratch, use a template, or upload the PDF they already use, and ask for a signature in one click.

media.name: therapy_5.png
media.title: A client’s profile, with assessment scores over time

layout.title: Progress you can see
text: Assessments like the PHQ-9 and GAD-7 go out every 30 days. Color-coded scores show how a client is doing since last time. Insurers increasingly ask for that data, so Headway rewards therapists who collect it.

layout.title: Result
text: The redesign shipped to tens of thousands of Headway therapists across all 50 states. The goal on every screen was the same: less time on admin, more time with clients.
